# CC17: 东宫门 Dong Gongmen

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC17` · Page: `/scenes/#CC17` · Row: `research/buildings/CC17-dong-gongmen/`

## What it was

东宫门 Dong Gongmen (大东门), the east gate of Changchun Yuan, reached from 鉴园 by a hill path: a seven-bay gate of two floors facing east, three-bay court rooms north and south, a moat with a stone bridge outside (S05 j83:18a; E0334, E0391). Jiaqing set out from it for the north in 1815-1820 (E0331-E0333). Malone repeats hearsay that Xianfeng left by it for Jehol in 1860 and that Cixi rebuilt it (E0392).

From the inventory row: **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S06, S01).

## What survives today

Malone (1934) reports stone lions and the bridge at the east gate (E0335, E0392). No dig of the east gate found; the 2001-04 gate-quarter report (S316) covers the south gate, not this one.

No excavation or survey of its remains found in this round.
